answers.answer: Select number of players + 1 Factory cards at random, place them face-down on the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose a structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts; play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘randomly select number of players + 1’; ‘11 marked territories’; ‘Randomly choose one structure bonus tile’; ‘The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.’

answers.answer: At setup, each character starts at its home base; two workers start, one on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining the home base. Four mechs begin over the four Faction Mat abilities, six stars by the faction emblem, six technology cubes in black-square green boxes, four structures in matching Player Mat boxes, four recruits in bottom-row circles, six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles, and the action token beside the Player Mat ready for placement. Starting power and combat-card draw come from the Faction Mat; starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards come from the Player Mat.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4: ‘Use the Faction Mat to set starting power and combat-card draw’; ‘Use the Player Mat to set starting popularity, coins and objectives’; starting-piece table/list.

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section each turn, but may take neither action (a legal dead turn), either action, or both. If taking both, take top before bottom; you cannot return to top afterward. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before the action, then choose as much or as little of exposed green-box benefits as desired. Exact costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades; use your mat. You cannot pay only part of a cost.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘different section’; ‘bottom first is not allowed’; ‘Rusviet may repeat’; ‘first pay the full cost’; ‘benefits need not all be taken.’

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure’s abilities; you retain those abilities even without control, except a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Pay action resources from any territories you currently control, even when taking the action elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls it’; ‘Enemy units do not gain your structure’s abilities’; ‘Pay costs using resources from any territories you currently control.’

answers.answer: No. On normal Move, you may move up to two different units one adjacent territory each; you cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice. All units can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources. Only mechs may also carry any number of your workers, never your character. A carried worker may subsequently move itself, or it may move onto a mech and be carried by that mech’s later move.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: ‘two different units, one adjacent territory each’; ‘cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice’; carried workers may subsequently move themselves.

answers.answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering a territory occupied only by enemy workers stops and cannot move again that turn. Those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leave resources behind, and you lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; having zero popularity does not prevent the retreat. It is not combat. Your own workers cannot independently move into a territory controlled by enemy workers.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops’; workers ‘immediately retreat’; ‘Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero’; worker independent-entry restriction.

answers.answer: After units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; complete movement of the other units first. The attacker chooses the order if there are multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: finish moving other units, then resolve combats ‘before the bottom-row action’; ‘attacker chooses multiple-combat order’; worker restriction on moving ‘into or out of’ enemy character/mech-controlled territory.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card, before upgrades; a built Monument also gives one popularity. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discards are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources, same or different, or one popularity, before upgrades; a built Armory also gives one power. Put traded resources on a controlled territory containing at least one worker. If all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Bolster: ‘Pay $1’; deck exhaustion rule. Trade: ‘any two resources … OR one popularity’; put resources on controlled territory with a worker; cannot Trade resources if all workers are home.

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity, and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token, placed on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village after payment. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Workers exposed during this Produce affect future Produce costs, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps 1–3: full cost before production; choose two territories; each worker produces; take new workers from Player Mat left to right after payment; new costs affect future actions.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs oil: move any technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs metal: put any chosen Faction Mat mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures, and recruits, you may still pay for that bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: ‘Upgrade — oil’; ‘Deploy — metal’; placement/effect restrictions; completed actions may still be paid for coins and recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Build costs wood. Place a structure from your Player Mat on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total may be on a territory, including opponents’ structures. Factory is allowed; lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A controlled Mill adds a Produce territory and produces as one worker in addition to actual workers; it cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Your Mine is a personal tunnel for your unit movement to and from it even while enemies occupy its territory, subject to ordinary entry/combat restrictions. Opponents cannot use your buildings’ abilities.
answers.evidence: Build — wood; one structure total, Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden; structures cannot move/destroy. Mill control exception and Mine tunnel rule.

answers.answer: When enlisting, take a recruit from any bottom-row section and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the selected one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is determined by the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, not by the one-time choice. For the rest of the game, when you or an immediate neighbor takes that corresponding bottom action, the bonus may trigger. Resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play, the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit goes to any open one-time space, bonus options, cannot later move; ongoing circle is where removed. Ongoing recruits: active, left, right sequence and two-player once rule.

answers.answer: Both combatants simultaneously and secretly select dial power from zero to the smaller of seven and their current power. They may each add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, including with zero dial power; Rusviet People’s Army adds one additional card total if workers are present. If both players have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously, add dial power and card values, and the attacker wins ties. Both players pay their dial power from the power track and discard every played card face-up; card values do not cost track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: ‘simultaneously and secretly’; dial limit; cards per participating character/mech; ability order; simultaneous reveal; attacker wins ties; both dial payments and card discard.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally up to two combat stars; Saxony may score without the usual limit within six available). Losing units—all characters, mechs, and workers—retreat to their home base, leaving all resources at the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie has the stated combat exception. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 4–5: winner controls and star; losing units retreat leaving resources; attacker popularity loss and defender exception; loser card draw condition.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve an encounter if the character remains on the token territory. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Discard the token and draw a card when resolving. Gains of resources, workers, mechs, or structures go to the encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no normal action cost or Player Mat benefit applies, including no ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Encounters: after Move and all combats; if contested entry is lost ‘the token stays’; gains go to encounter territory; ‘Pay no additional normal action costs’ and no mat/recruit benefits.

answers.answer: Every player’s character must choose one available Factory card on that player’s first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if necessary); this is not limited to the first visitor. Each player gets at most one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange it. A Factory card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom and the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception); its actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and normal movement/stop rules apply.
answers.evidence: Factory: ‘Every player’s character’ on first finish; at most one permanent card; fifth action section; no mat/recruit benefits; bottom Move distance and Speed.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective. You must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony retains the other card after the first and may score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: ‘Only on your own turn’; meet all requirements at reveal; place star and both cards on deck bottom; Saxony retains other card and can score both.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades; four deployed mechs; four built structures; four recruits; all eight workers on the board; one revealed completed objective; a combat victory (up to two stars, except Saxony); 18 popularity; or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony’s exception. Stars are permanent once placed even if power or popularity later falls, and other players’ stars do not block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends the game with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: full achievement list; goals awarded once; ‘A placed star is permanent’; other stars never block; sixth star immediately ends play.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing the star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement by returning initiating units to their prior territories; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, then resolve active player first, left neighbor, and right neighbor, checking for a sixth star at each step. If an earlier player places the sixth star, no later recruit star or bonus resolves.
answers.evidence: Sixth-star sequence: ‘primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing’; pending battle movement undone; active, left, right sequence and stop rule.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per controlled territory, and $2 per complete pair of controlled resources. Five stars add $20; four normal territories plus Factory count as seven territories and add $21; 13 resources make six complete pairs and add $12, total $53 in addition to held coins. The selected structure bonus is also scored, even if enemies control your structure territories. Tiebreakers, in order: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and example: ‘$20 + $21 + $12 = $53’; structure bonus even if enemies control; tie-break order.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea’s unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘A home base is not a territory’; default restrictions and exceptions; inactive expansion placeholders.

answers.answer: Mountain produces metal, tundra oil, farm food, forest wood, and village a worker. Lake and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; resources definition says workers are not resources; ‘Resource tokens have no supply limit: use multipliers if needed.’

answers.answer: All units can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources during movement; a mech may also carry any number of your workers, but never your character. A carried worker may move itself later in the turn. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, with the extra Speed step usable before or after it. A mech can pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Enemy-unit stops and character encounter stops override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move: unit carrying rules; Speed: adds one territory, tunnel jump costs one step, extra step before/after; stops override Speed.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit type.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit’; ‘Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure.’

answers.answer: You do not have to pay a partial Produce cost. If unable to afford any action, move your token to a different section and take neither action; this is a legal dead turn. You must move the token, and never pay only part of a cost.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘If unable to afford any action, take a dead turn’; ‘Never pay only part of a cost.’

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These are matching top-action bonuses. You keep a building’s abilities even without controlling its territory, and enemy units do not gain them, so an enemy occupant does not take them away.
answers.evidence: Bolster/Trade building bonuses; control section: ‘You keep those abilities even without control’; enemies do not gain them.

answers.answer: Riverwalk is for the character and mechs: Rusviet can enter farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Nordic forests and mountains; Polania villages and mountains; Saxony forests and mountains. Nordic Swim is the starting special ability for workers alone: they may cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes. It does not help Nordic character/mechs.
answers.evidence: Faction/Riverwalk table; Nordic Swim: workers alone cross rivers to land terrain, not lakes; does not help character/mechs.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including its Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. These shortcuts are for characters and mechs, not workers.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township descriptions both specify character/mech Move actions.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or Saxony’s Mine: the opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery may be used before combat by paying one power to reduce the opponent’s power by two, once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Saxony Underpass/Disarm and Nordic Seaworthy/Artillery ability descriptions.

answers.answer: Two mechs and three workers allow three combat cards total with Rusviet People’s Army: one additional card total when at least one worker is present, on top of the two cards allowed for two participating mechs. Workers alone never fight; a character or mech must participate.
answers.evidence: People’s Army: one additional card total, still requiring character/mech; ‘Two mechs and three workers allow three cards’; workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: With unlocked Wayfare, Crimea character/mechs may move from a territory or home base to its own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. They cannot enter an active opponent’s home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare: destinations include own or any inactive faction home base; ‘not an active opponent’s base.’

answers.answer: Before combat, Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets Crimea spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of the card’s value.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare/Scout and Crimea starting special ability Coercion descriptions.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and allows eligible units to retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers with them. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake, but gives no Nordic-style adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes need a mech to move off; carried workers and resources cannot be left behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy and Polania Submerge descriptions; lake-carried pieces rule and explicit Polania retreat limitation.

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not protect against popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Camaraderie: ‘after you win combat as aggressor on your turn’; does not protect against loss for undefended workers.

answers.answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. The first option’s gain can pay the second option’s cost. The summary does not say Polania may choose more than two options or waive a cost.
answers.evidence: Polania Meander: ‘up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain can pay second cost.’

answers.answer: A character entering an encounter-token territory during Factory bottom Move stops and cannot move again that turn. Encounters are resolved after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there; thus the encounter does not occur before all combats finish.
answers.evidence: Move encounter rule: character stops and cannot move again; resolve after whole Move action and all combats. Applies during Factory Move.

answers.answer: Combat-card count is public but card contents are secret; objective contents are secret. Coins are not hidden information, but a player need not reveal their total coin value. During combat, players may conceal whether they have committed cards until reveal.
answers.evidence: Setup information disclosure paragraph: public combat-card count, secret contents/objectives, coin totals need not be revealed, combat commitment may be concealed.

answers.answer: Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable in informal agreements; in tournament play even coin exchanges for deals or alliances are forbidden. Agreements are unenforceable. A payment cannot cancel combat once initiated by moving units onto opposing units: fight after Move, though bribes may influence the outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: ‘unenforceable’; ‘Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable’; combat cannot be canceled once initiated; bribes may influence outcome.

answers.answer: Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per controlled territory, $1 per complete pair of controlled resources. Popularity 7–12: $4 per star, $3 per territory, $2 per resource pair. Popularity 13–18: $5 per star, $4 per territory, $3 per resource pair. Controlled lakes count, home bases do not; a single leftover resource scores nothing because only complete pairs count.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table; controlled lakes count and home bases do not; ‘ignore an odd leftover token.’

answers.answer: For adjacency bonuses, count each qualifying feature only once across all your structures. Rivers do not break adjacency. Encounter locations count even after the encounter token has been removed. Tunnels are unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines; lakes are unique lakes. Payout for each bonus type (adjacent tunnels, lakes, or encounters): 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; 6 (or for lakes/encounters, 6–7) $9; zero features scores zero.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table: unique features, Mines excluded, removed encounters count, rivers do not break adjacency; listed tiers/payouts.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 $2; 2 $4; 3–4 $6. Structures in a row scores only your longest continuous straight line: 1 $2; 2 $4; 3 $6; 4 $9. Structures on farms/tundras counts qualifying structures combined: 1 $2; 2 $4; 3 $6; 4 $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table rows for structures on tunnels, structures in a row, and structures on farms/tundras.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
answers.evidence: Combat: attacker loses popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, ‘even for workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.’

answers.answer: A placed popularity star is permanent if popularity later drops, but current popularity determines final scoring tier. Yes, two factions may each earn a star for the same achievement: goals are once per player, and another player’s star never blocks the goal.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: ‘A placed star is permanent even if power/popularity later drops; current popularity still determines final scoring’; ‘Other players’ stars never block a goal’; ‘Each goal is awarded once.’

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seating matters because ongoing recruit bonuses can be triggered by you and your immediate left and right neighbors; their resolution order is active player, left neighbor, then right neighbor.
answers.evidence: Setup: randomly deal mats and seat factions in board order; Ongoing recruits: immediate left/right neighbors and resolution order.

answers.answer: Rivers are borders between land hexes; lakes are entire territories adjoining the surrounding shores. Units normally cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. Lake-capable character/mechs may move to/from lakes, but the summary does not specify from which particular surrounding land territories they may enter a lake; that detail is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘Rivers are borders between land hexes; a lake is an entire territory adjoining the surrounding shores’; unlocked abilities give exceptions. Seaworthy/Submerge specify lake movement generally.

answers.answer: No, the encounter card is not private: show it to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read its capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: ‘Show the encounter card to all players when drawn’, show artwork and read capitalized thematic text; no need to read every option.

answers.answer: No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.’

answers.answer: The next player may begin while the current player completes a noninteractive bottom-action decision; players may overlap that decision with the next turn. Interactive bonuses and game-end priority must still be resolved in order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Players may overlap a noninteractive bottom-action decision with the next turn, but resolve interactive bonuses and game-end priority in order.’

answers.answer: No. Each section’s top action and bottom action may each be taken at most once on that turn. The only stated repeat-section exception is Rusviet, which may repeat a section from last turn; that is a section-choice rule, not permission to repeat an action within the same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: take that section’s top action ‘once’ and bottom action ‘once’; Rusviet may repeat a section from last turn.

answers.answer: You may choose the alternative Move benefit and gain $1 instead of moving units.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: ‘Alternatively gain $1.’

answers.answer: No. The summary says workers never return to the Player Mat. New workers are taken from the mat left to right after Produce payment; forced retreats send workers to their home base, not the Player Mat.
answers.evidence: Produce: ‘Workers never return to the Player Mat’; retreat rules send workers to home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity, including both at zero.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘You may attack with zero power/popularity.’

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; you simply cannot earn further ordinary combat stars beyond that limit. Saxony has no usual limit within the six available stars.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit’; Saxony exception.

answers.answer: For an ordinary faction, you normally choose one affordable option; the summary does not allow declining to choose an option after drawing. You cannot select an unaffordable coin or popularity option. You must pay the chosen option’s printed cost, but may take as little of its benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: ‘Normally choose one affordable option’; must pay printed cost; may take as little benefit as desired; unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected.

answers.answer: No. Combatants choose their dials simultaneously and secretly, rather than in turn order. Dials and any played cards are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Combat step 1: ‘Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose’; step 3: ‘Reveal simultaneously.’

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: ‘Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.’

answers.answer: No. Star goals are placed as soon as achieved, and the sixth star immediately ends play. An objective is different: a completed objective may be held and revealed later, but only on your own turn and only while all its requirements are met at reveal.
answers.evidence: Stars: ‘Place a star as soon as you achieve’; sixth star immediately ends play. Objectives: ‘You may wait’ to reveal a completed objective.

answers.answer: Normally no. Units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes; unlocked abilities provide exceptions. The summary identifies Nordic Swim as a worker-only river crossing ability, and lake movement exceptions for specific character/mech abilities.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘Units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes. Unlocked abilities give exceptions below.’

answers.answer: No. The recruit is permanently placed on the Faction Mat one-time bonus space and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: ‘put it permanently’ on a bonus; ‘It cannot later move.’

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter. A mech or worker entering the territory does not resolve the encounter or remove its token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: ‘Only a character triggers an encounter.’

answers.answer: A controlled Mill provides one additional Produce territory, beyond the up to two chosen controlled territories, and the Mill itself produces as one worker in addition to actual workers there. It can produce even when no actual worker is on its territory. If you do not control the Mill territory, it cannot produce.
answers.evidence: Produce: controlled Mill ‘provides an additional bonus production territory and itself produces as one worker’; can work without actual worker; only while controlled.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. If your last unit leaves and you have no structure, resources alone do not establish control; control requires a unit or qualifying structure presence.
answers.evidence: Control: ‘You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit.’

answers.answer: Build costs wood; Enlist costs food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row resources: ‘Upgrade — oil; Deploy — metal; Build — wood; Enlist — food.’
